primary.title: CDSL Q2 results: Net profit jumps 24% YoY to Rs 173 crore, revenue up 24%
primary.description: Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL), a market infrastructure institution, on Saturday reported a 24% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 173 crore in the second quarter, compared with Rs 140.2 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.Revenue grew 23.7% to Rs 395 crore from Rs 319 crore in the year-ago period. EBITDA increased to Rs 229 crore, while EBITDA margin expanded to 58% from 56% a year earlier.For the quarter under review, CDSL opened around 75 lakh new demat accounts during the quarter, taking its assets under custody (AUC) beyond Rs 89 lakh crore. The company's demat account base registered year-on-year growth of around 17% as of the end of Q2, Vora said.Commenting on the performance, Nehal Vora, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of CDSL, said participation in India's securities market continued to remain resilient despite global macroeconomic volatility. The company's demat account base grew around 17% year-on-year as of the end of Q2.He added that the sustained growth in market participation would encourage CDSL to further strengthen its operations and value proposition.During the quarter, CDSL increased its investments in India International Bullion Holding IFSC Limited (IIBHL) to support the development of IT infrastructure, among other initiatives.The company also made a strategic investment in the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), an initiative of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.Separately, CDSL's subsidiary, Centrico Insurance Repository Limited, signed a software development partnership agreement with Shoveltech Solutions Private Limited, a company operating in the health-tech domain.CDSL facilitates the electronic holding, settlement and transfer of securities, catering to various market participants, including depository participants, issuers, investors, registrars and transfer agents (RTAs), clearing corporations and stock exchanges. It is Asia's first listed depository and manages over 19.34 crore demat accounts, with a network of more than 590 depository participants.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. primary.title: Dalal Street Weak Ahead: Nifty stands on firmer footing, but can it break past 23,450?
primary.description: The Indian equity markets staged a strong recovery during the week, reversing part of their recent losses and ending on a positive note. The Nifty began the week on a relatively subdued footing but witnessed buying interest at lower levels, helping the Index recover and close above the psychologically important 23,000 mark. The trading range remained relatively wide, with the Nifty oscillating in a 730.75-point range. Volatility eased considerably; the India VIX declined by 9.25% to 15.30, reflecting some moderation in market uncertainty. The headline Index ended the week with a net gain of 453.10 points (+2.00%).135396555The most significant technical development during the week was the Nifty's ability to reclaim its 200-week Moving Average, presently placed at 22,700.18. This is an important positive development, especially after the index slipped below this long-term trend indicator. However, the broader technical structure remains vulnerable, and the recent recovery should not yet be interpreted as a confirmed trend reversal. The 200-week MA is now expected to serve as the principal reference point for the markets over the coming weeks.The Nifty's ability to defend this level on a sustained basis will be crucial in determining whether the present recovery develops into a more meaningful upward move. Conversely, a renewed breach of this average would weaken the recovery attempt and leave the Index exposed to further downside pressure.135398740The coming week is likely to see the markets attempting to consolidate their recent gains, with a cautiously positive undertone. The levels of 23,300 and 23,450 are likely to act as immediate resistance points. The supports are expected to come in at 22,750 and 22,525.The weekly RSI stands at 43.29; it stays neutral and does not show any divergence against the price. The weekly MACD remains bearish and trades below its signal line. A big white candle at the 200-week MA reinforces the credibility of this support point.135398772The pattern analysis of the weekly chart shows that the Nifty is presently attempting to stabilize near an important long-term support confluence. The 200-week MA coincides closely with a trendline support drawn from the major lows of early 2025, making the 22,700 zone technically significant. The immediate challenge for the Nifty will be to sustain above the reclaimed support while negotiating the overhead supply zones. The 20-week Bollinger Band midpoint, presently at 23,696.04, represents an additional resistance area.In the coming week, market participants should approach the markets with cautious optimism but avoid adopting an aggressively bullish stance. The recovery above the 200-week MA is encouraging, but the absence of stronger momentum confirmation warrants a measured approach. Fresh buying should remain selective. It would also be prudent to protect gains after sharp rebounds instead of chasing prices at higher levels. A stockspecific approach, disciplined risk management, and close monitoring of the Nifty's behavior around its 200-week MA should remain the central strategy for the coming week.In our look at Relative Rotation Graphs, we compared various sectors against the CNX500 (NIFTY 500 Index), representing over 95% of the free-float market cap of allthe listed stocks.The Relative Rotation Graph (RRG) shows a distinct change of leadership in the markets.The Nifty Sector Index has rolled inside the leading quadrant. The Nifty Bank, Media, Pharma, and IT Indices are inside the leading quadrant as well. These groups are likely to relatively outperform the benchmark.The Metal Index has sharply rolled back inside the weakening quadrant. The Realty, Midcap100, and the Auto sector Indices are also inside the weakening quadrant.Only Nifty FMCG and Energy Sector Indices are inside the lagging quadrant. However, both of these are seeing a sharp improvement in their relative momentum against the broader markets.The Nifty Infrastructure Index has rolled inside the improving quadrant. The PSE, PSU Bank, and the Financial Services Indices are also inside this quadrant. They may see an overall improvement in their momentum against the broader Nifty 500 Index.Important Note: RRG™chartsshow the relative strength and momentum of a group ofstocks. In the above Chart, they show relative performance against the NIFTY500 Index (Broader Markets) and should not be used directly as buy or sell signals.

primary.description: Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL), a market infrastructure institution, on Saturday reported a 24% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 173 crore in the second quarter, compared with Rs 140.2 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.Revenue grew 23.7% to Rs 395 crore from Rs 319 crore in the year-ago period. EBITDA increased to Rs 229 crore, while EBITDA margin expanded to 58% from 56% a year earlier.For the quarter under review, CDSL opened around 75 lakh new demat accounts during the quarter, taking its assets under custody (AUC) beyond Rs 89 lakh crore. The company's demat account base registered year-on-year growth of around 17% as of the end of Q2, Vora said.Commenting on the performance, Nehal Vora, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of CDSL, said participation in India's securities market continued to remain resilient despite global macroeconomic volatility. The company's demat account base grew around 17% year-on-year as of the end of Q2.He added that the sustained growth in market participation would encourage CDSL to further strengthen its operations and value proposition.During the quarter, CDSL increased its investments in India International Bullion Holding IFSC Limited (IIBHL) to support the development of IT infrastructure, among other initiatives.The company also made a strategic investment in the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), an initiative of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.Separately, CDSL's subsidiary, Centrico Insurance Repository Limited, signed a software development partnership agreement with Shoveltech Solutions Private Limited, a company operating in the health-tech domain.CDSL facilitates the electronic holding, settlement and transfer of securities, catering to various market participants, including depository participants, issuers, investors, registrars and transfer agents (RTAs), clearing corporations and stock exchanges. It is Asia's first listed depository and manages over 19.34 crore demat accounts, with a network of more than 590 depository participants.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. primary.title: Dalal Street Weak Ahead: Nifty stands on firmer footing, but can it break past 23,450?
primary.description: The Indian equity markets staged a strong recovery during the week, reversing part of their recent losses and ending on a positive note. The Nifty began the week on a relatively subdued footing but witnessed buying interest at lower levels, helping the Index recover and close above the psychologically important 23,000 mark. The trading range remained relatively wide, with the Nifty oscillating in a 730.75-point range. Volatility eased considerably; the India VIX declined by 9.25% to 15.30, reflecting some moderation in market uncertainty. The headline Index ended the week with a net gain of 453.10 points (+2.00%).135396555The most significant technical development during the week was the Nifty's ability to reclaim its 200-week Moving Average, presently placed at 22,700.18. This is an important positive development, especially after the index slipped below this long-term trend indicator. However, the broader technical structure remains vulnerable, and the recent recovery should not yet be interpreted as a confirmed trend reversal. The 200-week MA is now expected to serve as the principal reference point for the markets over the coming weeks.The Nifty's ability to defend this level on a sustained basis will be crucial in determining whether the present recovery develops into a more meaningful upward move. Conversely, a renewed breach of this average would weaken the recovery attempt and leave the Index exposed to further downside pressure.135398740The coming week is likely to see the markets attempting to consolidate their recent gains, with a cautiously positive undertone. The levels of 23,300 and 23,450 are likely to act as immediate resistance points. The supports are expected to come in at 22,750 and 22,525.The weekly RSI stands at 43.29; it stays neutral and does not show any divergence against the price. The weekly MACD remains bearish and trades below its signal line. A big white candle at the 200-week MA reinforces the credibility of this support point.135398772The pattern analysis of the weekly chart shows that the Nifty is presently attempting to stabilize near an important long-term support confluence. The 200-week MA coincides closely with a trendline support drawn from the major lows of early 2025, making the 22,700 zone technically significant. The immediate challenge for the Nifty will be to sustain above the reclaimed support while negotiating the overhead supply zones. The 20-week Bollinger Band midpoint, presently at 23,696.04, represents an additional resistance area.In the coming week, market participants should approach the markets with cautious optimism but avoid adopting an aggressively bullish stance. The recovery above the 200-week MA is encouraging, but the absence of stronger momentum confirmation warrants a measured approach. Fresh buying should remain selective. It would also be prudent to protect gains after sharp rebounds instead of chasing prices at higher levels. A stockspecific approach, disciplined risk management, and close monitoring of the Nifty's behavior around its 200-week MA should remain the central strategy for the coming week.In our look at Relative Rotation Graphs, we compared various sectors against the CNX500 (NIFTY 500 Index), representing over 95% of the free-float market cap of allthe listed stocks.The Relative Rotation Graph (RRG) shows a distinct change of leadership in the markets.The Nifty Sector Index has rolled inside the leading quadrant. The Nifty Bank, Media, Pharma, and IT Indices are inside the leading quadrant as well. These groups are likely to relatively outperform the benchmark.The Metal Index has sharply rolled back inside the weakening quadrant. The Realty, Midcap100, and the Auto sector Indices are also inside the weakening quadrant.Only Nifty FMCG and Energy Sector Indices are inside the lagging quadrant. However, both of these are seeing a sharp improvement in their relative momentum against the broader markets.The Nifty Infrastructure Index has rolled inside the improving quadrant. The PSE, PSU Bank, and the Financial Services Indices are also inside this quadrant. They may see an overall improvement in their momentum against the broader Nifty 500 Index.Important Note: RRG™chartsshow the relative strength and momentum of a group ofstocks. In the above Chart, they show relative performance against the NIFTY500 Index (Broader Markets) and should not be used directly as buy or sell signals.

clusters.description: Thiruvananthapuram: The Vizhinjam International Seaport on Saturday received its first import container, marking a significant step towards emerging as a direct gateway for imports into Kerala, port authorities said.The container, booked from Ningbo in China, arrived aboard the vessel MSC Sabrina III.The flag-off ceremony of the first import container was performed by Vizhinjam International Seaport Ltd Managing Director Jeromic George, according to an official statement.The container was booked by Thiruvananthapuram-based startup BSG Logistics and Ship Chandlers Pvt Ltd on behalf of the city's Altair Group. primary.title: Vizhinjam port receives 1st import container
primary.description: Thiruvananthapuram: The Vizhinjam International Seaport on Saturday received its first import container, marking a significant step towards emerging as a direct gateway for imports into Kerala, port authorities said.The container, booked from Ningbo in China, arrived aboard the vessel MSC Sabrina III.The flag-off ceremony of the first import container was performed by Vizhinjam International Seaport Ltd Managing Director Jeromic George, according to an official statement.The container was booked by Thiruvananthapuram-based startup BSG Logistics and Ship Chandlers Pvt Ltd on behalf of the city's Altair Group. It carries engineered building boards used in the construction sector as an alternative to conventional plywood.With the commencement of import operations, goods can now be directly unloaded at Vizhinjam, undergo customs clearance and be transported to markets across Kerala.This is expected to reduce dependence on other ports and cut down the time and cost involved in cargo movement, authorities said.The new facility will also help retain revenue generated from cargo handling and logistics-related activities within the state, instead of such business flowing to other ports.It is also expected to generate employment opportunities in Thiruvananthapuram and other southern districts in areas such as customs brokerage, freight forwarding, transportation, warehousing and port-related operations.The commencement of direct import services marks an important expansion of Vizhinjam's role beyond transshipment operations, positioning it as a port catering directly to the import requirements of businesses in Kerala, the authorities added.
